title: Electoral College: From Election Day to Inauguration
learningObjectives: Explain how the popular vote is used to appoint electors who later vote for President and Vice President.
Describe the sequence of certification, elector voting, and transmission of electoral votes.
Identify the role of Congress in counting electoral votes and the final transfer of office on Inauguration Day.

explanations.text: Voters do not directly elect the President; the popular vote determines which electors a State will appoint.

evidence.quote: The States use these general election results (also known as the popular vote) to appoint their electors.

events.label: Election Day – Voters Help Determine Electors

evidence.quote: During the general election your vote helps determine your State's electors.
By December 11, 2024—States issue Certificates of Ascertainment
Your State's Executive prepares seven Certificates of Ascertainment.
The electors meet in their respective States and vote for President and Vice President on separate ballots.
Electoral votes must be received by the President of the Senate and the Archivist no later than the fourth Wednesday in December.
Congress meets in joint session to count the electoral votes.

predictions.prompt: Which happened first: Election Day or Congress counting the electoral votes?
